prompt: A dropped object has fallen $s(t) = 5t^2$ meters after $t$ seconds. Use the limit $\lim_{h \to 0} \frac{s(2 + h) - s(2)}{h}$ to find its instantaneous velocity at $t = 2$ seconds, in meters per second.
hint: Instantaneous velocity is the limit of average velocities over shorter and shorter time windows starting at $t = 2$.

hints.text: Instantaneous velocity is the limit of average velocities over shorter and shorter time windows starting at $t = 2$.
$s(2 + h) = 5(4 + 4h + h^2) = 20 + 20h + 5h^2$ and $s(2) = 20$. Subtract, then divide by $h$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Shrinking stopwatch windows
steps: The averages settle at $20$ m/s — the speedometer reading at the instant $t = 2$.
